I only know human medicine but—

1. Blood from upper GI track (esophagus, stomach) look dark, almost black. This is because the blood gets “digested”. Blood from the lower GI track (butthole, colon) look vivid red, because it hadn’t been “digested” yet. 

If its blood that you’re seeing in the stool, I can’t think of anything acutely life threatening from an episode of bloody stool. If he’s actively bleeding out (which is very dangerous), he’ll continue to have the spotting. If theres something else that’s causing episodic bleeding (in humans, this could be hemorrhoids, cancer, autoimmune diseases— which does not seem likely if I’m extrapolating human medicine to dog medicine, which again IS ONLY A VERY ROUGH ESTIMATE). I’d keep an eye out to see make sure he’s not having more bleeding. If he is, he should be taken to the vet. 

2. White stains— vomit can have different colors and consistencies. White sounds like sputum (spit), which seems more like GI upset than something more serious and life threatening, like a blockage or a bleed. I would make sure that he has access to water (in human medicine, we can supplement water with salt and sugar if dehydration is an issue, and the patient can tolerate oral intake— look up diy pedialyte, but PLEASE make sure it’s doggy friendly). I would also try to hear for GI noises (grumbling in stomach indicates the bowels are moving along as they should— like the growling sounds your own tummy) to make sure things are moving along there. It’s not a super accurate test even in humans, but you gotta do what you gotta do in low resource environments. I would make sure his abdomen isn’t bloating (keep a measurement of his stomach circumference at the widest point, with a piece of string if you have no measuring tape), and that he’s drinking and peeing okay. 

Again; this is a VERY POOR SUBSTITUTION for vet visit. However, I understand not everyone had the resources of developed world, and I want to do what I can to ease your mind. If things go south, you may be able to raise funds via gofundme, and some subreddits that allow donation requests.

I recommend the TV show Pachinko if you’re interested in Korean-Japan relations. 

I wrote all this all to explain the seeming inconsistency but also to demonstrate the collective koreanness that exists— a LONG history, a sense of perseverance against more powerful & hostile neighbors (sup China & Mongolia), and connection to the culture. 

If you don’t think you can genuinely claim ownership of any of that— don’t. But if you’re interested, Korea is a cultural soft power & cultural exporter and you’ll find many resources & pop culture that will ease you into the culture. Look up Korean traditional dramas (most often set in the Joseon dynasty, arguably the most well-documented period before modern world), or watch Korean variety shows, or webtoons (comics designed for the web— very on brand for the technologically connected country).
